items.title: A world of reflections
items.subtitle: Sphereflake · procedural geometry
items.description: Five levels of recursively arranged spheres become a landscape of reflections. Environment mapping, soft shadows and a checkered floor reveal structure at every scale.
items.alt: Glossy blue-gray spheres repeat into tiny clusters and reflect a black-and-white checkered floor.

items.title: See through the assembly
items.subtitle: Acrylic ball bearing
items.description: An ordinary bearing becomes an optical study. Transparent races reveal the rolling elements inside, while reflections and refraction describe the shape of the complete solid assembly.
items.alt: A transparent acrylic ball bearing, its concentric races and spherical rolling elements visible against black.

items.title: Growth, expressed in geometry
items.subtitle: Parametric nautilus
items.description: A growing elliptical aperture sweeps along a logarithmic spiral to make a closed, ray-traceable shell. One parametric generator produces this nautilus and several other shell forms.
items.alt: A pearly shell coils inward through successively smaller smooth whorls on a black background.

items.title: Every blade of grass is geometry
items.subtitle: Stryker · path-traced scene, 2004
items.description: An archival demonstration of full-scene light transport: a detailed vehicle sits among modeled foliage and grass. The image records 11,542,992 triangles and eight trillion rays, rendered with ADRT/RISE on 2004 hardware—not a present-day performance claim.
items.credit: 2004 U.S. Army Research Laboratory · BRL-CAD documentation
items.alt: A detailed Stryker vehicle with slat armor in a grassy scene with trees; the original render statistics remain visible along the bottom.

items.title: One strut. A whole structure.
items.subtitle: Geodesic space frame
items.description: A single strut prototype is instanced along the unique edges of a geodesic sphere. Joint spheres complete an intricate space frame without individually modeling every member.
items.alt: A silver spherical lattice formed by many interlocking triangular struts.

items.title: Inside a mathematical surface
items.subtitle: Voxelized gyroid · cutaway
items.description: Sampling a three-dimensional scalar field turns a repeating gyroid into volume geometry. A cutaway exposes its internal passages; the blue companion demonstrates an extruded height field from the same workflow.
items.alt: An orange cutaway gyroid volume reveals repeated winding passages beside a blue extruded height-field block.

items.title: Connected, without intersecting
items.subtitle: Interwoven torus chainmail
items.description: Individual torus rings thread through their neighbors to form a woven sheet. The generator varies tube thickness and color across the pattern, demonstrating an assembly of interlocking solid parts.
items.alt: An open sheet of interwoven rings transitions from orange in the middle to blue around its edges.

items.title: A world within the world
items.subtitle: Earth cutaway · archive selection
items.description: A removed wedge opens the globe into nested solid layers, bringing otherwise hidden volumes into view. Surface mapping contrasts with the exposed interior in this historical illustration—not a scientific scale model.
items.credit: Historical BRL-CAD gallery · individual creator unrecorded
items.alt: A textured Earth has a large wedge removed, exposing concentric brown, yellow and metallic-looking interior layers.

items.title: An everyday object, revealed
items.subtitle: Transparent pen · archive selection
items.description: A transparent housing reveals the refill, spring and internal mechanism of a familiar pen. Rather than cutting the object apart, the rendering lets us see how its components fit together.
items.credit: Historical BRL-CAD gallery · individual creator unrecorded
items.alt: A pen runs diagonally across a neutral background; its clear housing reveals a yellow refill, coiled spring and gray internal mechanism.

renderModes.title: Shaded
renderModes.description: Material color, direct lighting, shadows and reflection.
renderModes.alt: Cornell-box scene with a red wall, a blue wall, two gray blocks and direct illumination.

renderModes.title: Surface normals
renderModes.description: Color encodes surface direction, making orientation changes visible.
renderModes.alt: The same Cornell-box scene colored pink, green, cyan and purple according to surface orientation.

renderModes.title: Edges
renderModes.description: A line rendering isolates silhouettes and visible edges.
renderModes.alt: The same Cornell-box scene drawn as white outlines on black.

renderModes.title: Surface coordinates
renderModes.description: A vivid test map shows surface coordinates: red tracks U, blue tracks V. This reveals mapping independently of material appearance.
renderModes.alt: The same Cornell-box scene with magenta, purple and blue gradients revealing surface coordinates.
